newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel wins $222 mln Asian telecoms deal.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel wins $222 mln Asian telecoms deal.

text.p: French engineering group Alcatel said on Tuesday it won a $222 million contract for the major part of an undersea telecommunications network in Asia.

The new link will be owned by 90 telecommunications carriers and will span some 11,000 kms when completed at the end of 1998. The link will be an extension of the South East Asia-Middle East-Western Europe Number Three (SEA-ME-WE 3) network for which contracts were awarded in January.

The Alcatel Submarine Networks unit will supply the undersea system for the southern part of the new network and supply the synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) equipment and network management for the whole system.
Alcatel said it would be supplying the world's largest international SDH network, allowing communications between up to 40 landing points between Germany and Japan.
The new link through the South China and East China Seas will increase the total length of the SEA-ME-WE 3 network to 38,000 km and will be the longest undersea network installed to date, it said.
